scenes.heading: Semi-Structured Data
scenes.narration: Semi-structured data has some organizing tags or keys, but it does not enforce a rigid, fixed schema like a relational table.

scenes.heading: Characteristics
bullets: Self-describing tags or keys, like JSON fields
Common in APIs and event streams
scenes.narration: Semi-structured data is self-describing because keys or tags label each value. Its structure is flexible and can evolve without breaking everything downstream. It often nests data in hierarchies, which relational tables handle poorly. This flexibility is why it is so common in APIs and event streams.

scenes.heading: A semi-structured JSON record
scenes.narration: This JSON-style record shows why we call the data semi-structured. It has clear keys like user_id and name, so it is not chaotic, yet it also nests an object under prefs and a list under tags. Reading a nested value means walking into that hierarchy, as the last line does. This mix of labels and flexibility is the defining trait of semi-structured data.

scenes.heading: Structured vs semi-structured
scenes.narration: Structured data enforces a rigid schema when data is written, keeping everything flat and uniform. Semi-structured data instead carries its structure with the data itself and is interpreted when read. That makes it far more adaptable when data shapes change over time.

scenes.text: Semi-structured data trades rigid schemas for flexibility, which is ideal for evolving APIs and events.
scenes.narration: In practice, semi-structured formats give engineers flexibility to handle evolving and nested data without a rigid upfront schema.
